slides.title: HAMPO Launches WiFi and Bluetooth Enabled Ego Camera Module for Untethered Embodied AI Data Collection
slides.highlight: The launch of a WiFi and Bluetooth enabled ego camera module supports untethered data collection for embodied AI, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: LLM-Assisted Behavioural and Scenario Augmentation for Agent-Based Energy Adoption Models
slides.tldr: LLM-ASSISTED BEHAVIOURAL AUGMENTATION FOR ENERGY ABMS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a hybrid framework integrating LLMs into agent-based models to enhance behavioural assumptions and scenario analysis, aligning with MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: A hybrid framework using LLMs to design bounded behavioral rubrics and scenarios for energy adoption ABMs.
card.key_idea: LLMs generate offline, rule-validated behavioral multipliers and techno-economic scenarios that augment, rather than replace, a calibrated logistic adoption model for solar PV adoption by dairy farms.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 500 Monte Carlo worlds and five seeds across multiple policy settings; results showed stable, monotonic adoption increases up to 13% over baseline.
card.limitation: Rubrics are structured approximations rather than empirical measurements; LLM is used offline, avoiding live inference or adaptive agent evaluation.

slides.title: SocioGesture: Real-Time and Adaptive Social Gesture Perception for Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: SocioGesture enables robots to recognize social cues like invitations and refusals in real-time, supporting the HRI goals of RwB.

card.one_liner: SocioGesture provides real-time, occlusion-robust social gesture recognition for robots with an uncertainty-driven offline adaptation loop.
card.key_idea: A lightweight dual-stream body-hand skeleton model using confidence-aware encoding and occlusion-aware training, paired with a cloud-based video model for offline vocabulary expansion.
card.evaluation: Tested via LOSO cross-validation on a custom HRI dataset and live Unitree G1 deployment; showed high robustness to joint occlusion and real-time edge latency.
card.limitation: Cannot recover information from severe occlusions and requires offline human verification for scalable, safe vocabulary adaptation.

slides.title: Establishing a Dynamic Multimodal HRI Dataset for Engagement Analysis with a Humanoid Robot
slides.highlight: This work proposes a protocol for a multimodal dataset integrating physiological signals, behavioral data, and self-reports to analyze user engagement with humanoid robots, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Proposed experimental design for a multimodal HRI dataset to analyze user engagement during collaborative tasks.
card.key_idea: A synchronized data-collection protocol integrating physiological signals (EDA, PPG), human/robot IMU data, vision (RGB-D, LiDAR), and subjective questionnaires across three levels of task complexity.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper describes a proposed protocol and planned recruitment of 30 participants, but no results are reported.
card.limitation: The research is currently at the conceptual design stage; data collection and implementation are listed as future work.

slides.title: Realbotix Testing Humanoid Robots at Live Events
slides.highlight: Realbotix is testing humanoid robots for crowd presentations, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Reinforcement Learning for Sequential Solar PV Policy Design under Uncertainty: An Agent-Based Approach
slides.highlight: This research integrates reinforcement learning with a stochastic agent-based model to optimize solar PV adoption policies, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent-based impact analysis.

card.one_liner: RL-driven adaptive policy design optimizes solar PV adoption and public cost trade-offs using agent-based simulations.
card.key_idea: Integrates PPO, SAC, and TD3 algorithms with a stochastic agent-based model to learn sequential policy interventions (grants, loans, tariffs) via a scalarised reward framework.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Irish dairy farm data over 16-year horizons using 300 stochastic episodes; compared against static baseline policies across three RL algorithms.
card.limitation: Limited to one geographic context, a 16-year horizon, and simplified adoption behaviors that omit certain financial and implementation constraints.

slides.title: Development of a Humanoid Robot Prototype for Multimodal Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This prototype integrates gesture recognition, object detection, and LLM-based voice processing, providing a flexible testbed for embodied social interaction relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: An affordable, 3D-printed humanoid robot prototype for multimodal HRI using gesture, voice, and vision AI.
card.key_idea: A 14-DOF humanoid integrating MediaPipe/LSTM for gestures, YOLO for 3D object localization, and LLM-based semantic parsing for voice commands via a Jetson AGX Xavier.
card.evaluation: Validated via pick-and-place tasks and social interactions; achieved 96% gesture accuracy, 92% speech accuracy, and average positioning error of 1.83 cm.
card.limitation: Reliance on external LLM APIs introduces latency and requires constant internet connectivity.

slides.title: TEIDAN: A Multilingual Multiparty Dialogue Corpus
slides.highlight: This corpus of multimodal three-party conversations supports research on addressee recognition and turn-taking, contributing to the multimodal social perception goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: TEIDAN is a multilingual multimodal corpus of spontaneous three-party face-to-face discussions in Japanese and English.
card.key_idea: The corpus uses pin microphones, microphone arrays, and cameras to record triadic open-ended discussions, providing IPU-based transcripts for cross-linguistic analysis of turn-taking and multimodal grounding.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via descriptive quantitative statistics (IPU/turn duration) and qualitative sequential analysis of turn construction across 69 sessions.
card.limitation: Differences in participant relationships (acquainted Japanese speakers vs. stranger English speakers) may confound cross-linguistic and cultural comparisons.

slides.title: Mind the Gap: Theory-of-Mind-Grounded Friction for Epistemic Alignment
slides.tldr: THEORY-OF-MIND GROUNDED FRICTION FOR EPISTEMIC ALIGNMENT
slides.highlight: This work proposes a Theory-of-Mind (ToM) inference method to detect silent divergence in belief states between participants. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and the perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: ToM-grounded friction improves LLM intervention and calibration in collaborative dialogues by modeling second-order beliefs.
card.key_idea: Operationalizes Theory-of-Mind via a four-part belief schema to compute 'friction' signals, which then condition Frictive Policy Optimization (FAR and FTR variants).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on HCRC MapTask using intervention F1, ECE, and Brier scores; FAR/FTR outperformed DPO in stability and calibration.
card.limitation: Friction-based preference pairing (FPP) failed by intervening indiscriminately, showing friction must regulate behavior at the instance level.
